title: snapshot --parts refuses an empty or repeated part name
findings_note: s383 relay report 2026-10-22, later note: `--parts ''` or a trailing comma gives a usage message naming an empty part, and `--parts items,items` merges silently
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the part list itself, the revision hash, and the other `snapshot` options.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `cmd_snapshot` (`src/slicer/cli.py`) splits `--parts` on commas and refuses a name that is not in `snapshot.PARTS`. An empty value or a trailing comma yields an empty name, so the usage line reads "unknown snapshot part(s) " with nothing after it and the person cannot tell what was wrong. A repeated name (`--parts items,items`) is accepted and the part is built once, so the request and the answer differ without a word. A dashboard script that builds the list by joining names gets either result with no hint.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli_report.py` (`cmd_snapshot`, where `args.parts` is split; the spec named `cli.py`).
- `tests/test_snapshot.py`, next to `test_Snapshot_Parts_OnlyNamedParts`.
- `docs/agents.md` (the `snapshot` contract, the `--parts` errors), `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Snapshot_EmptyPartName_UsageNamesIt`: `snapshot --json --parts ''` and `--parts items,` exit 2 with a usage message that says the part name is empty, and print nothing on stdout.
- `test_Snapshot_RepeatedPart_Usage`: `--parts items,items` exits 2 with a usage message naming `items` as repeated, and prints nothing on stdout. The owner settled it on 2026-11-08: refuse, do not collapse.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. In `cmd_snapshot`, refuse an empty name and a repeated name before any project is read, as exit 2 with `usage`, in the same stderr form as the unknown-part message.
3. Update `docs/agents.md` and the CHANGELOG.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
